prophet_vs_baseline.note: Positive improvement means Prophet's fleet-mean WAPE across the rolling backtest folds is lower than the best baseline's. A negative value is reported as-is -- it means the baseline measurably won on this data.

replenishment_backtest_ewma.methodology: 18 evaluation point(s), every 10 days across the last 180 days, each recomputed with ingredient_forecast()'s own `now` parameter using only data that existed at that point, checked against real ledger balances 7 days later.

false_alarm_breakdown.note: 'resolved_by_restock': a real purchase_receipt ledger row landed for that exact ingredient within the check window -- the flag's own lead-time logic is what that window is keyed to, so this is at least as consistent with the warning having been acted on as with it being wrong. 'genuine': no such receiving event occurred, yet the ingredient never actually hit zero -- the model overestimated risk with no restocking to explain why.

observable_windows.note: Same as `confusion`, but skips evaluation points whose 7-day check window recorded under 25% of a normal week's orders (a data-collection gap or closure). With no trading, no stock outcome can have been driven by demand, so a flag there is neither confirmed nor refuted. `confusion` above still includes them.

within_window_label.note: Stockout = balance <= 0 at any point inside the check window (what the docstring has always claimed), instead of only at its end. Same flags, same forecasts.

any_warning.note: Positive = critical, out OR at_risk, against the same end-of-window label. at_risk means 'depletes after the lead time but within lead + review cycle' -- ordering today still prevents it, so it is not part of the primary flag.

replenishment_backtest_ewma.adjusted_precision_note: Excludes false_alarm_breakdown.resolved_by_restock from the false-alarm count -- see that field's note. critical_flag_precision above is kept unchanged alongside this for comparison.

fpgrowth_expanding_window.methodology: Three nested expanding-window folds over the same real 365-day dataset (~180d train / next ~60d test, ~240d train / next ~60d test, ~300d train / remaining ~65d test), boundaries placed against real calendar dates present in the data. A pair is checked against every fold whose test window was not already part of the training data that first identified it. See this module's EXPANDING_FOLD_DEFS / stability-rule comment for the fixed validated_stable / unstable_failed / insufficient_evidence rule, decided before any fold was evaluated.
